rationale: The source carries two independent obligations with different activation. (1) Bind-before-Ratify: an open plan session (which may start with no issue) must be bound to a local ATDD issue slug before confirm, so the plan is authored as that issue's PLANNED substrate on its registered branch + worktree; this is what the validator and the PlanSession.confirm() guard enforce. (2) Modify loop (term modify_loop): after commit, a validator failure re-opens the session for operator adjustment and re-author; it fires on a different trigger (post-commit validator failure), in a later phase, with different evidence. The previous single rewrite only failed on an invented 'no ratchet baseline' in a shared strict-disposition node; here disposition 'strict' is repeated verbatim in each part's verifier_detail and no shared node is used, so nothing is added to it. Round 2: S003 (kind) is now traced to each part's audit entry 'kind: rule' instead of an invalid ':kind' dest.

fires: Planner starts an atdd plan session with no pre-existing issue or brief (allowed; binding is required only before confirm).

doesNotFire: Work unrelated to an atdd plan session (e.g. coder GREEN changes on an already-planned issue).

parts.given: An atdd plan session has a decomposition. It may have started with no pre-existing issue or brief.
parts.when: You Ratify (confirm/lock) the decomposition and author the plan.
parts.then: Before confirm, bind the decomposition to a local ATDD issue record (a target issue's manifest/State Store slug, or one minted from the main job), then author the plan as that issue's PLANNED-phase substrate on its registered branch + worktree.
prefer: Start conversationally and decompose before any issue paperwork; no pre-existing issue or brief is needed. Bind any time before confirm.
`atdd plan session bind-issue --id <sess> --issue <slug>`; list bindable slugs with `atdd coach issues open`, or mint one from the main job.
Bind by the local manifest/State Store slug; the GitHub number is a synced projection added later.
avoid: Reading 'no up-front ceremony' as 'no issue at all'. The session removes the ceremony, not the issue.
Confirming an unbound decomposition, or authoring plan substrate on an untracked branch (no issue + branch + worktree).
Waiting for, or binding by, a GitHub issue number.
parts.why: The iron rule (issue + branch + worktree per repo modification) must always hold, even with no GitHub, so plan substrate always lands on a tracked branch tied to a local issue.
evidence: PlanSession.confirm() raises until self.issue_ref is set.
Plan substrate is authored on the bound issue's registered branch + worktree as PLANNED-phase substrate.
verifier_detail: Binding identity is the LOCAL manifest/State Store record slug (#945/#1168), not a GitHub issue number. GitHub is a downstream extension that syncs the number after install; the slug is GitHub-agnostic and the GitHub number is a synced projection.

The session must refuse to lock (confirm) a decomposition not bound to an ATDD issue, so plan substrate is never authored on an untracked branch. Guard: PlanSession.confirm() raises until self.issue_ref is set.
audit: supersedes: planner.plan.in-session-no-issue. Corrects the earlier in-session-no-issue framing, which wrongly read as 'no issue at all'.

parts.given: A plan was ratified and its substrate committed.
parts.then: Re-open the plan session, adjust the plan with the operator, and re-author it.
prefer: Make the adjustment together with the operator inside the re-opened session.
avoid: Leaving the validator failure unresolved instead of re-opening the session for adjustment and re-author.
parts.why: The session's modify loop is how plan defects caught after commit are corrected: through operator adjustment and re-author.
evidence: After a post-commit validator failure, the session is re-opened and the plan is re-authored after operator adjustment.
